newsitem.title: HONG KONG: More widespread HK warrants may follow bourse move.
newsitem.headline: More widespread HK warrants may follow bourse move.

text.p: A recent rash of warrant issues on Hong Kong's leading stocks may spread to other counters following the Stock Exchange of Hong Kong's implementation of a ballot system for warrant issues, analysts said.
But with only very few stocks close to their maximum warrant issue level, the impact may be minimal, they added.
The Exchange said last Friday it would allot shares to warrant issuers by ballot if the number of shares available was insufficient for all interested parties to issue warrants.
"It is possible that issuers switch to other stocks, resulting in little change to the number of warrants being issued but more stocks being covered," said ASG Investment analyst Michael Ng.

About 58 warrant issues have been launched so far in January, including 28 last week. The issues have helped drive the Hang Seng index to new record highs, with issuers of covered warrants having to buy the underlying stock, brokers said.

Despite the slew of issues, only Hopewell Holdings Ltd has already reached the maximum limit and seven warrant issues this month involving China Travel International Investment Hong Kong Ltd have brought that stock close to the maximun level, analysts said.
According to the exchange regulations, covered warrants cannot exceed 30 percent of the public float of the stock involved.
One source from a warrant issuer said the move was a short term measure which the exchange had imposed following the recent flurry of issues.
"I think the number of warrant issues will come back down later when the market gets quieter," he said.
Brokers said the measure might also serve to stabilise the market.
